meta.angle: Magnet and field physics for the catalog's magnet systems (QD PPMS 14/16 T, DynaCool 9/12/14 T, Oxford TeslatronPT 8/12/14 T and 6/1/1 T vector, Lake Shore CRX-VF 2.5 T)
meta.status: proposals only; no catalog, physics, experiment or Lean file was modified
meta.division_free: Every relation is lhs <= rhs over +, -, * of dimensioned quantities; irrational constants (pi, mu0) enter only through rational bounds; sufficient-only conditions are encoded through the validity list, so no Lean change is required.
meta.coordination: Does not duplicate the parallel workflow (datasheet values/absences, cooling-power curves, envelope/cryogen/pressure/stress tables, interval representation, QuickXplain, SiLA/OPC UA). MAG-2 supplies magnet semantics and sources for the envelope model; table import stays with the envelope workflow.

findings_about_current_model: magnet_ramp_time (status validated) passes on a necessary-only bound: B_target <= (dB/dt)_max * t_budget uses a lower bound on the ramp time (the model's own assumption), and QD's documented times to full field exceed it by x1.07 (9 T), x1.25 (12 T) and x1.71 (14 T DynaCool), contradicting the assumption text 'times to full field are consistent with field / maximum rate'.

lakeshore_crx_vf records magnetic_field.max = 2.5 T for 10-420 K, but the manufacturer table (already in evidence ev_ls_0004) gives 2.5 T only at 10 K, 2 T for 11-400 K and 1 T for 401-420 K; independent checks of field and temperature can therefore pass combinations the instrument cannot reach.
The CRX-VF magnet is a superconducting solenoid (vertical field, current control), not an electromagnet.
oxford_teslatronpt_6_1_1T_vector stores the 6 T main-axis rating as magnetic_field.max next to vector = true, so profiles needing more than 1 T off the main axis could pass.
Five QD uniformity values exist in evidence (ev_qd_0040-0042, ev_qd_0057, ev_qd_0058) but are UNKNOWN in the configurations because the 'ppm' key cannot carry the region length and center height.

magnetic_field.max is the field at the magnet center, which QD places about 4 cm above the standard transport-puck surface; QD Tech Note 1084-312 shows the puck-surface field is lower (about -5 % for the 16 T PPMS by reading its figure) and recommends the vertical puck or rotator for transport at the center.
QD's classic PPMS brochure (1070-002 Rev. C1) prints '14 T: 100 Oe/s (≈1 T/min.)', internally inconsistent (100 Oe/s = 0.6 T/min); the catalog correctly stores 100 Oe/s.
On liquid-helium PPMS systems full field is recommended only above 60 % helium (14 T magnet: 1 T at 40-60 %; 16 T magnet: 0 T), a field limit that depends on run duration through helium consumption.

The DynaCool magnet is switch-less (driven only), so persistent-mode creep does not apply there; remanent (trapped-flux) offsets of tens to ~200 Oe after high-field excursions do apply to QD magnets and matter for the VSM profile's 1 kOe M(T) step.

proposals.title: Make magnet_ramp_time sound: keep the max-rate inequality as a fail-only (necessary) check and add a sufficient pass check from documented time-to-full-field or field-banded rate tables
proposals.description: The validated model magnet_ramp_time passes whenever B_target <= (dB/dt)_max * t_budget. Its own assumption says the max-rate time is a lower bound on the real ramp time, so the inequality is only NECESSARY: its violation soundly rejects, but its satisfaction does not establish that the target is reached in time. QD's data show the gap is real: the DynaCool 14 T at 100 Oe/s needs >= 1400 s, but QD documents 'less than 40 min (typical)' = 2400 s to full field (ratio 1.71; 12 T: 1200 s vs 1500 s, ratio 1.25; 9 T: 450 s vs 480 s, ratio 1.07), so the model's assumption text 'Quantum Design's times to full field are consistent with field / maximum rate' is contradicted for the 14 T magnet. Ramp rates are also field-banded in practice: QD's EverCool guidance ramps to 8 T at full rate and 8-9 T at 100 Oe/s; Oxford's MercuryiPS applies coercive rate-limit tables by current band (example 10 A/min to 70 A, 8 A/min above). Physical cause: AC losses heat the winding and lower the quench current as the ramp rate rises (Caspi 1983); in cryocooler-cooled magnets such as DynaCool and TeslatronPT this heat must be removed by the cryocooler (Liu 2005). Proposal: split the model into (1) the existing relation, now documented as a fail-only necessary bound, and (2) a sufficient pass relation encoded through the validity list so it can only PASS or give NEED INFO: (A, assumption-free) t_full,doc <= t_budget with B_target <= B_max (monotone ramp from zero reaches any lower field no later than full field); (B, optional, only if the reviewer accepts 'documented rate is non-increasing with field') B_target * t_full,doc <= B_max * t_budget; (C) when a banded table (B_0=0 < B_1 < ... with rates r_i) is documented, the exact multiplied-out banded time, e.g. for two bands B_1*r_2 + (B_t - B_1)*r_1 <= t_budget*r_1*r_2. The sufficient half needs the approach mode to be Linear (Oscillate overshoots by about 30 % and takes longer). No Lean change is needed: a sufficient-only condition is expressed by putting it in 'validity' and repeating one validity bound as the relation.
proposals.equation_latex: \text{fail iff } B_t > \dot B_{\max}\, t_b;\qquad \text{pass if } t_{\mathrm{full}} \le t_b \wedge B_t \le B_{\max};\quad\text{(rate non-increasing in }B\text{): } B_t\, t_{\mathrm{full}} \le B_{\max}\, t_b;\quad\text{banded, }B_1 \le B_t \le B_2:\ B_1 r_2 + (B_t - B_1)\, r_1 \le t_b\, r_1 r_2
proposals.validity: 0 <= B_target <= B_max of the installed magnet; ramp from zero field in Linear approach mode (no Oscillate/No-Overshoot overhead); one monotone ramp; t_full,doc is QD's 'typical' time to full field (manufacturer specification class, as already accepted for pm_021-pm_023); banded form only inside the documented band B_{k-1} <= B_target <= B_k (re-checked by Lean as validity bounds); assumption B only with reviewer sign-off.

proposals.title: Validate field_temperature_envelope as division-free temperature bands; fix the CRX-VF 2.5 T over-statement; add the liquid-helium PPMS helium-level field limit
proposals.description: magnetic_field.max and temperature requirements are checked independently, so the CRX-VF (catalog 2.5 T, 10-420 K) passes e.g. '2.2 T at 300 K', but Lake Shore documents ±2.5 T only at 10 K, ±2 T for 11-400 K and ±1 T for 401-420 K (this table is already in the catalog as ev_ls_0004). Encode a documented envelope as bands (T_lo,i, T_hi,i, B_i): for every band overlapping the profile's operating temperature(s) emit B_req <= B_i with validity T_lo,i <= T_op <= T_hi,i (selected by the serializer like cooling_power.at_*, re-checked by Lean; a temperature in an undocumented gap such as 10.5 K gives NEED INFO, never PASS). For QD and Oxford the documented envelope is rectangular: QD says the magnet 'is always at the same temperature' and the classic PPMS magnet 'is always immersed in liquid helium'; the VSM option's operational range is '1.8 to 400 K; 0 to 16 T'; the TeslatronPT VTI gives 1.5-300 K 'while operating the magnet'. For the liquid-helium PPMS (14 T, 16 T) QD adds a third axis: full field only with helium above 60 %, 1 T (14 T magnet) or 0 T (16 T magnet) at 40-60 %, so a run needing more than 1 T for t_run couples to the cryogen-consumption model: h_0 - hdot*t_run >= 60 %. This is the magnet-physics part of the envelope work; importing further envelope tables belongs to the separate envelope-table workflow.
proposals.equation_latex: \forall i:\ T_{lo,i} \le T_{op} \le T_{hi,i} \Rightarrow B_{\mathrm{req}} \le B_i;\qquad\text{LHe PPMS: } B_{\mathrm{req}} > 1\,\mathrm{T} \Rightarrow h_0 - \dot h\, t_{\mathrm{run}} \ge \tfrac{60}{100}

proposals.title: Position-resolved field at the sample: axial profile (standard puck surface vs magnet center) and (delta, L, z_c) homogeneity regions, filling 5 UNKNOWN uniformity entries
proposals.description: magnetic_field.max is the field at the magnet center. QD places the magnet center about 4 cm above the transport-puck surface (the VSM coil center, 4.05 cm), and QD Tech Note 1084-312 plots the 'relative change in field between the puck surface (A) and the center of the magnet (B)'; its table tells users of ETO, Resistivity and AC Transport to 'use Vertical Puck or Rotator option' (heat capacity: Vertical Puck) to reach the center. Read from its Fig. 1 (approximate, not printed numbers): about -5 % at the puck surface for the 16 T PPMS, -0.8 % for 14 T PPMS, -0.35 % for 14 T DynaCool, -0.2 % for 9 T PPMS, about 0 for 9 T DynaCool. Separately, uniformity is documented as pairs (delta over L, centered at z_c): DynaCool 9 T ±0.01 % over 3 cm, 12/14 T ±0.1 % over 5.5 cm; PPMS 14 T ±0.1 % over 5.5 cm, 16 T ±0.1 % over 1.0 cm; all five are UNKNOWN in the catalog because the 'ppm' key cannot hold the length; the CRX-VF has radial pairs 0.5 % over 10 mm and 1.0 % over 25 mm diameter (vertical field, perpendicular to the sample). Proposal: (i) store uniformity as {delta (dimensionless), L (m), z_c (m above puck surface), geometry axial|radial}; (ii) give each measurement option a sample position (center | puck_surface | height in m), taken verbatim from 1084-312's table; (iii) necessary-and-sufficient field check at the sample B_req <= r_pos * B_max (r_center = 1 by definition; r_puck from QD's tabulated profile once obtained); (iv) a sufficient-only homogeneity check: the sample's axial span, including the VSM vibration amplitude A, lies inside the documented region and delta_doc <= delta_req; it never fails because a datasheet uniformity is an upper bound and a smaller region can be more uniform (quadratic scaling to smaller regions is unsound, see rejected ideas).
proposals.equation_latex: B_{\mathrm{req}} \le r_{\mathrm{pos}}\, B_{\max};\qquad \text{pass if } 2(z_s - z_c) + L_s + 2A \le L_{\mathrm{doc}} \,\wedge\, 2(z_c - z_s) + L_s + 2A \le L_{\mathrm{doc}} \,\wedge\, \delta_{\mathrm{doc}} \le \delta_{\mathrm{req}}\ (\text{else NEED INFO});\quad \text{radial: } D_s \le D_{\mathrm{doc}} \wedge \delta_{\mathrm{doc}} \le \delta_{\mathrm{req}}
proposals.validity: Axial specs are on-axis values for a sample centered on the bore axis; z measured above the standard puck surface; VSM: A = peak vibration amplitude (2 mm typical) and sample length L_s per the catalog's eg_017 (< 5 mm); radial (CRX-VF) specs apply in the sample plane at the field center; r_puck values only from a QD table or a documented digitization with uncertainty; profiles may state delta_req only as user-entered (published procedures do not).

proposals.title: Vector-field region for the 6/1/1 T magnet: per-axis ratings as a necessary box, rotation sphere and single-axis ratings as sufficient regions
proposals.description: oxford_teslatronpt_6_1_1T_vector stores magnetic_field.max = 6 T (main axis) plus magnetic_field.vector = true, so a profile asking for, e.g., 2 T in the sample plane with vector capability would pass although the transverse axes are rated 1 T. Vector magnets have coupled limits: Meckler et al. report 5 T / 1.3 T in single-axis mode but only 3.5 T / 1 T in cooperative mode; Oxford states for its vector rotate magnets 'Full spherical rotation at the lowest rated axis' and a typical tilt of only 2.5 degrees at the maximum-field axis; a commercial 6/1/1 T magnet offers '1 Tesla spherical vector rotation'. Proposal: capabilities magnetic_field.axis_{x,y,z}.max (single-axis ratings) and magnetic_field.rotation.max (radius r_rot of the documented full-rotation sphere); profiles state the required field as axial (one axis), rotation (magnitude B in every direction of a set) or a general vector set. Division-free relations (squares remove signs): necessary box Bx^2 <= Bx,max^2, By^2 <= By,max^2, Bz^2 <= Bz,max^2 (fail-capable); sufficient sphere Bx^2+By^2+Bz^2 <= r_rot^2 and sufficient single-axis region (other components exactly 0, |B_i| <= B_i,max), both encoded through validity so they only PASS or give NEED INFO. For a rotation requirement of magnitude B: NOT MET if B^2 > min_i B_i,max^2, MET if B^2 <= r_rot^2.
proposals.equation_latex: \text{fail if } B_x^2 > B_{x,\max}^2 \vee B_y^2 > B_{y,\max}^2 \vee B_z^2 > B_{z,\max}^2;\quad \text{pass if } B_x^2 + B_y^2 + B_z^2 \le r_{\mathrm{rot}}^2 \ \text{or}\ (B_x = B_y = 0 \wedge B_z^2 \le B_{z,\max}^2);\quad \text{rotation of }|B|: \text{fail if } |B|^2 > \min_i B_{i,\max}^2
proposals.validity: Field components in the magnet frame; single-axis region only when the other components are exactly zero; r_rot only from a vendor statement for this magnet (Oxford's Proteox rule is an analog, not TeslatronPT evidence); the 2.5 degree tilt cone needs a rational inner bound on tan(2.5 deg) and a TeslatronPT source before use; the serializer instantiates only the region matching the declared requirement kind and Lean re-checks it, so a wrong choice can only give NEED INFO.

proposals.title: Low-field accuracy after high-field excursions: remanent (trapped-flux) field and persistent-mode creep as a sufficient-only check
proposals.description: QD systems report the field computed from magnet current. After a high-field excursion, flux pinned in the windings leaves an error at low set fields: up to 20 G (9 T magnet) and 120 G (14 T) in linear mode (1070-207), up to ~200 Oe for a 16 T magnet (1500-021), about 100 Oe for the Nb3Sn 14 T magnets and generally < 10 Oe for NbTi magnets up to 9 T (1096-301); setting zero in Oscillate mode from above 1 T typically leaves 1-2 G; in persistent mode the field at the sample drifts by ~20-25 G within about an hour after discharge, an effect removed by staying in driven mode. Nb3Sn magnets have larger error fields (Lu 2019); the artefact is visible in published remanent-magnetization data (Bud'ko 2026). The VSM profile measures M(T) at 1 kOe after M(H) up to 9 T: the field error is 2 % for a 9 T magnet and up to 12 % for a 14 T magnet in Linear mode, but 0.2 % after Oscillate. Model: B_rem,bound(magnet, approach mode) + [persistent only] B_creep <= eps * B_set, valid for B_set <= 1 T, sufficient-only (documented values are 'up to'/'typically' upper bounds, so the check can only PASS or give NEED INFO). DynaCool is switch-less (driven only), so the creep term is zero there.
proposals.equation_latex: B_{\mathrm{rem}}(\text{magnet},\text{mode}) + \mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{persistent}}\, B_{\mathrm{creep}} \le \varepsilon\, B_{\mathrm{set}}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{pass, else NEED INFO};\quad \text{valid if } B_{\mathrm{set}} \le 1\,\mathrm{T}
proposals.validity: Low-field regime B_set <= 1 T (QD: deviations matter below 1 T); a previous excursion above 1 T; bounds per magnet class (NbTi <= 9 T vs Nb3Sn >= 14 T) and approach mode (Linear vs Oscillate vs Low Field option); classic PPMS values transfer to DynaCool only as 'QD instruments' statements (1500-021) - otherwise inferred.

proposals.title: Replace the unsupported temperature_stability_during_field_sweep with an eddy-current + Joule heat budget during field sweeps
proposals.description: A field sweep induces eddy currents in conducting sample holders and cold fingers inside the bore. For a thin disk (thickness h much smaller than the skin depth) of radius R and conductivity sigma in a uniform axial field ramped at dB/dt, P = (pi/8) sigma h R^4 (dB/dt)^2 (Tan 2014, after Knoepfel). Add this term to the existing Joule model: I^2 R_s + P_eddy <= P_cool(T_doc), using the same cooling-power slot and validity as joule_heating_vs_cooling_power. pi is irrational, so use rational bounds (333/106 < pi < 22/7): the pass relation uses 22/7 and an upper bound on sigma (user-entered low-temperature value), the fail relation uses 333/106 and a lower bound on sigma (the room-temperature value, 5.96e7 S/m for copper, since a pure metal's conductivity rises on cooling). A conservative quasi-static validity mu0 sigma h R (dB/dt) <= B_target (eddy time constant shorter than the ramp) keeps the thin-disk formula in range. For liquid-helium PPMS magnets with a persistent switch, QD notes that the switch dissipates V^2/R during ramps (V = L dI/dt), which is the same (dB/dt)^2 coupling on the helium bath; that extension waits for the cryogen-consumption data.
proposals.equation_latex: 8 I^2 R_s + \pi_{\uparrow}\, \sigma_{\uparrow}\, h\, R_d^4\, \dot B^2 \le 8\, P_{\mathrm{cool}}(T_{\mathrm{doc}}) \Rightarrow \text{pass};\quad 8 I^2 R_s + \pi_{\downarrow}\, \sigma_{\downarrow}\, h\, R_d^4\, \dot B^2 > 8\, P_{\mathrm{cool}}(T_{\mathrm{doc}}) \Rightarrow \text{fail};\quad \pi_{\downarrow} = \tfrac{333}{106},\ \pi_{\uparrow} = \tfrac{22}{7};\quad \text{valid if } \mu_0\, \sigma_{\uparrow}\, h\, R_d\, \dot B \le B_t \wedge T_{\mathrm{doc}} \le T_{\mathrm{op}}
proposals.validity: Thin conducting disk normal to a uniform field; quasi-static ramp; all dissipated power reaches the stage whose cooling power is used (as in the Joule model); T_doc <= T_op (cooling power documented at or below the operating temperature); sigma_down = 300 K value is a valid lower bound only for pure normal metals (also in field, where copper's magnetoresistance stays far below its room-temperature resistivity for RRR >> 1 - needs a source before the fail side is enabled).

citations.quote: DynaCool is supplied with the sample chamber block thermometer MR calibrated, so temperature values reported by the base DynaCool are always corrected for magneto-resistance. However, some option thermometers are supplied without an MR calibration.

proposals.risks: Calibration state is per unit and can change; 'a few percent' at 9 T is not a number, so the uncorrected bound is only usable above 14 T (> 5 %) as a lower bound.

rejected_ideas: Scaling a documented uniformity to a smaller region with the leading solenoid term (delta(L) = delta_doc (L/L_doc)^2): unsound for compensated magnets whose axial profile is not monotone (counterexample f = z^2 - z^4: max 0.25 over |z| <= 1 but 0.1875 over |z| <= 0.5, where the scaling predicts 0.0625). Homogeneity is therefore pass-or-NEED-INFO only (MAG-3).

Using the per-axis ratings of the 6/1/1 T magnet (box) as a sufficient condition: unsound, combined fields are limited below the single-axis ratings (Meckler et al. 2009: 5 T vs 3.5 T; Oxford: about 2.5 degree tilt at the main axis). The box is kept only as the necessary (fail) side of MAG-4.

A high-field persistent-mode decay model (ppm per hour): no catalog magnet documents a decay rate; the DynaCool is switch-less, Oxford's vector rotate magnets are driven-only, Bluefors offers a persistent switch only as an option ('higher stability', no number); only zero-field creep (~20-25 G after discharge, QD 1070-207) is documented, folded into MAG-5.

An inductive-voltage ramp limit L*dB/dt <= k*V_max: magnet inductance and field constant are documented only for a typical 9 T PPMS (about 35-40 H, 1950 Oe/A), not for any catalog configuration, and the documented maximum rates already embed this limit.

A separate persistent-switch heating model for the liquid-helium bath (P = V^2/R, QD 1099-205): only relevant to liquid-helium/EverCool PPMS and only useful together with helium consumption data that the cryogen workflow is researching; recorded as an extension of MAG-6 and MAG-2 instead.

Turning QD's advice to measure at stable fields between -2 T and +2 T with 14 T or higher magnets (flux-jump noise, QD 1096-301) into a NOT MET rule: it is a data-quality recommendation, not a feasibility limit; keep it as advisory text in the VSM explanation.

Encoding QD AR10 (magnetic force on the PPMS probe above 1 T near ferromagnetic objects affects temperature control below 10 K) as a requirement: it is a site-installation condition (1 m from rebar walls), not a property of a configuration.

Using the CPX-VF manual's power-supply limits (0.12 A/s maximum ramp, 35 A maximum current) for the CRX-VF: a different, older product and no field constant is printed, so the conversion to T/s would be a cross-product inference.
Treating the BAQIS facility page ('Magnet ramp to full field: <= 60 minutes') as a TeslatronPT manufacturer specification: it is a third-party restatement; at most inferred_estimate.
Using the demonstrated 0.3 T/min sweep of a 12 T TeslatronPT Plus as a maximum rate: an achieved rate is a lower bound on capability, so it can support a PASS but never a NOT MET.

Entering the field ratios digitized from QD Tech Note 1084-312 Fig. 1 as trusted evidence: they are read from plotted curves, not printed values; they stay inferred_estimate until QD supplies the tabulated profile it offers on request.
Accepting a 'lambda-plate' or sub-4.2 K requirement for the 16 T PPMS: searched (WebSearch) and found no Quantum Design document stating it; the only lambda-plate statements concern Oxford magnets.

Substituting the DynaCool Horizontal Rotator (-10 to 370 degrees) for vector-magnet capability in the mK vector-transport profile: the rotator cannot reach 50 mK; mechanical rotation is worth modelling later as a magnetic_field.direction capability for angle-dependent transport profiles above 1.8 K.

Applying Bluefors catalogue magnet maxima (16 T solenoid, 9 T vector) to the LD configurations: no LD-specific compatibility table exists (already UNKNOWN in the catalog) and Bluefors magnets are outside this angle's systems.
